properties.title: Hornocker Cabin
properties.description: The Hornocker Cabin was constructed in 1952 by Jess and Dorothy Taylor. It was later named after Maurice Hornocker who conducted research on Mountain Lions. The duplex is now used as an office space on one side, and a living space on the other.

properties.title: Bridge Crossing Big Creek
properties.description: Bridges across Big Creek used to be old swinging bridges. In the 50s and 60s, the USFS began replacing the old bridges with steel span bridges. The bridge segments were flown to Taylor Ranch.

properties.title: Taylor Airstrip
properties.description: Jess Taylor began constructing the Taylor Ranch airstrip in May of 1948. It took him approximately one year to complete the project due to the amount of brush and trees he had to remove. Jess used a team of 1,800 pound geldings and dynamite to remove the remaining stumps for the new landing strip.

properties.title: DeVlieg Cabin
properties.description: The biggest facility at TWRS was funded by the DeVlieg foundation after the loss of a bunkhouse and cookhouse that burned in 2000 (Diamond Complex Fire). Due to a large majority of the trees in the are burning, all of the materials to build the cabin had to be flown in.

properties.title: Lanham Cabin
properties.description: The Lanham cabin originally was located on the Cabin Creek homestead. After finding out that the USFS was going to naturalize the site. Jim Akenson began planning how to transport the cabin to TWRS. His original plan was to float the logs down to Taylor. However, the U of I got in contact with the Idaho National Guard Engineering Division which ended up flying pieces of the cabin to TWRS as part of their summer training maneuvers in a Chinook chopper in June 1990.

properties.title: Hay Barn
properties.description: Built in the August of 1985 by Jim Akenson and crew. A lot more went into the building of this hay barn than what meets the eye. Corner and wall posts were floated down Big Creek and then lifted out of the water by a pulley system. A mule team and stoneboat sled were used to move them to the building site. The site was on an old junkyard which had to be cleaned up along with removing the 400 pound boulders in the area. The rest of the building materials were flown in via three trips from Moscow.

properties.title: Dave Lewis Cabin
properties.description: In 1910, John Conyer built a cabin a long Big Creek. After moving upriver to Cabin Creek, Dave Lewis moved into the cabin which he lived in until his death in 1936. It was restored in 2008 through funding from three donors.

properties.title: Cookhouse
properties.description: The cookhouse is the newest building on the property. It is a community space used by students as a gathering space and for cooking.

properties.title: Arlow Lewis Cabin
properties.description: This cabin was inhabited by Arlow Lewis who was hired by the University of Idaho as a caretaker in 1970. The cabin is now used by Idaho Fish and Game employees who operate the rotary screw trap in Big Creek.

properties.title: Taylor Cabin
properties.description: The Taylor Cabin was built in 1951 by Jess and Dorothy Taylor. It is now used as the caretaker cabin.

properties.title: Bridge over Pioneer Creek
properties.description: This bridge crosses over Pioneer Creek which is the water source for Taylor.

properties.title: The Orchard
properties.description: The orchard produces several varieties of apples in the fall and cherries in the summer.
